desc:
To translate product pages and keep your style, Ecom Swift LLC translates titles, descriptions, collections and key policies into the languages you choose, follows your glossary of brand terms and loads the finished text into your store.

## What does it mean to translate product pages and keep your style?

It means the translated page reads as if it had been written in that language, while still sounding like your brand. A literal word-for-word version often reads stiffly, mangles product names or uses a tone that does not fit. A good translation keeps your meaning, your names and your voice.

For a store, translation covers more than product descriptions. Collection pages, menu labels, shipping and returns text, and order emails all belong to the shopper's experience in their own language.

## Why language changes whether people buy

Shoppers trust pages written in their own language. They can read specifications, understand return terms and feel sure that a real business stands behind the store. A page in a second language that is only partly translated, or that sounds odd, makes people wonder about the rest of the store.

Language also affects search. People search in their own words, so a properly translated page can match queries that an English page never would. Results depend on the market, the competition and your delivery options, but a store that speaks to people clearly has a better chance of earning their order.

## What a good translated store includes

- Product titles and descriptions translated for meaning and natural reading.
- A glossary of brand and product names that must stay as written.
- A tone matched to your original copy, whether it is warm, direct or formal.
- Collection pages and menu labels translated so navigation makes sense.
- Shipping and return policy text in the shopper's language.
- Order and shipping email templates translated.
- Size and unit conversion, such as inches to centimeters, where it applies.
- Correct language settings in your store, so each visitor sees the right version.
- Search titles and meta descriptions translated for each page.
- A check by a native speaker on key pages in the larger package.

## How we work

We begin with your glossary: the names of products, ranges and features that should not be translated, plus any terms that need a fixed equivalent. We also note the tone you want and the market you are targeting, because wording for a formal market differs from wording for a casual one.

We then translate in batches, starting with your best selling products, and keep a consistent vocabulary across every page. Sizes, units and date formats are adjusted for the market. Items that depend on local rules, such as legal wording in policies, are marked for your review.

The Basic package adds one language for a first set of products, with the glossary, as a sheet. The Standard package covers up to two languages, translates collections and menus, loads the text into your store and converts sizes and units. The Premium package covers up to three languages, translates your shipping and return policies and order emails, and includes a native speaker check of the key pages. An extra check of hreflang tags and search settings is available as an add-on.

## What to do, and what to avoid

**Do:**
- List the names that must never be translated.
- Pick languages based on where you can actually ship.
- Translate policies, not only product pages.
- Have a native speaker read your most important pages.
- Keep original and translated text in sync when products change.

**Avoid:**
- Translating only half of a page, which looks unfinished.
- Leaving prices, sizes and units unadapted.
- Using machine output without any human review.
- Adding languages you cannot support with customer service.
- Translating brand names that shoppers already know.

## Who this is for

It suits a store that already sells well in one language and wants to open a new market. It suits a seller whose customers in another country keep asking for a translated site. It also suits a brand preparing a multilingual launch with a limited range.

## What we need from you

Send a product export, your glossary or brand notes and the languages you want. Tell us which pages matter most. We never need your password: access to your store is given as a collaborator, staff or developer user with limited permissions, and you can review every translation before it goes live.
